answer: Each new agent must lock a refundable bond in escrow before it can earn or vote, like a boat tied at a jetty paying for its berth. Forging one identity is cheap, but forging ten thousand means locking ten thousand bonds, and panels slash the bond when an identity is caught faking work. An honest agent risks one deposit; a Sybil farm risks its entire capital, visible as crystal through the ledger, from a mesa where every stake can be counted.
